findings.description: The bucket has no ACL restricting access and is commented as being public, meaning anyone could read/write the objects it holds, including sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects (including the customer-master.xlsx file) are stored unencrypted at rest.
No versioning block is configured, allowing objects to be overwritten or deleted without recovery, increasing risk of data loss/tampering going undetected.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data stored unencrypted and publicly accessible
findings.description: A sensitive customer master file is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is unencrypted and publicly accessible, exposing PII/financial data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving it unencrypted at rest.
No versioning is enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of financial records cannot be recovered.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so operations data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, leaving data science bucket contents unencrypted at rest.
